intro.heading: Civil Contracting Workflow Problems Begin at Three Points
intro.body: BOQ revisions that never make it back into the budget. Subcontractor bills reconciled from memory. RA bill certification without a measured record to check against. Handled by hand, these three points are where civil contracting margins quietly disappear.

personas.title: Attendance Tracked in Registers That Get Lost or Faked
personas.body: Manual registers are filled in by supervisors, sometimes from memory. Workers who left early or never showed up still get marked present, and payroll disputes follow every month.

personas.title: Equipment Idle Time and Asset Losses Across Sites
personas.body: Without a live view of where equipment is deployed, machines sit idle on one site while another site rents the same category at cost. Losses and idle time are only noticed at month-end reconciliation.

personas.title: Quality Issues Discovered Late, Causing Expensive Rework
personas.body: Quality checks that live in a supervisor's notebook do not get escalated until the defect is already built over. Rework at that stage costs far more than catching the issue during execution.

personas.title: RA Bills Certified Without a Measured Record
personas.body: Running account bills get certified against a subcontractor's claim because there is no independent measurement to check it against. Overbilling passes through and is rarely recovered.

personas.title: BOQ Revisions Never Reflected in the Working Budget
personas.body: Scope changes get agreed verbally on site and the BOQ is revised on paper, but the budget that finance is tracking against never gets updated, so cost control runs on stale numbers.

personas.title: Daily Progress Reports Delayed or Skipped Entirely
personas.body: DPRs get filed a week late from memory, or not filed at all when a site is busy. By the time the office sees a delay or quality flag, the window to act on it has already closed.

features.title: GPS and Face-Verified Attendance Across Every Site
features.body: Workers check in from the SiteFlow mobile app with GPS location and face recognition confirming they are physically on site. Management sees live headcounts per site and per contractor as attendance is recorded.

features.title: Track Material Against the BOQ, Not Against Memory
features.body: Every material issue is recorded against the BOQ line it belongs to, so procurement, wastage, and consumption are visible in real time instead of surfacing as one number at project close.

features.title: Daily Progress Reports Without the WhatsApp Chase
features.body: Site engineers submit DPRs from the mobile app the same day work happens, with photos and quantities attached. The office sees delays and cost issues as they happen, not days later.

Delay and quality flags visible to the office same-day

faqs.q: What is civil contracting software and how is SiteFlow different from a spreadsheet?
faqs.a: Civil contracting software brings planning, budgets, resource tracking, and documentation into one system. Unlike a spreadsheet, SiteFlow updates automatically from real site records, GPS attendance, material issues, and RA bills post directly against the budget instead of being re-entered by hand.

faqs.q: How does SiteFlow keep BOQ revisions in sync with the working budget?
faqs.a: Each budget line maps to a BOQ item. When a revision is approved, it updates the working budget directly, so the numbers finance is tracking against always reflect the current scope.

faqs.q: Can SiteFlow certify RA bills against actual measured work?
faqs.a: Yes. Subcontractor claims are checked against site-measured quantities before an RA bill is certified, so overbilling is caught before payment rather than disputed after.

faqs.q: Does SiteFlow work across multiple civil sites at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes. Contractors managing several sites see progress, material usage, attendance, and cost from one consolidated dashboard, with drill-down to any individual site.
